    Lemma 3.7 for the categorical filtration #

    projective-rays.tex (lem:ray-degree): "Write F^nA(x,y) = J^n(P_y,P_x) […] Every space A₀(x,y)_d of degree d has dimension at most one, and initial forms give a bijection between the nonzero rays of A and the nonzero spaces A₀(x,y)_d. If the endpoint subbimodules satisfy U_{r'} ⊊ U_r, then deg_J(r') > deg_J(r)."

    The proof only uses that the filtration is multiplicative, starts at A, ends at zero, and contains the radical in degree one ("endpoint radicals belong to J"). We prove the lemma for every positive filtered deformation P of a graded algebra Λ with this property (PosFiltration.RadOne): the corner layers have dimension at most one (finrank_corner_le), elements of one degree lie in one ray (ray_eq_of_degree), a smaller subbimodule has a larger degree (degree_lt_of_lt), and the initial form σ_d maps the corner F^dA(x,y) onto the corner Λ(x,y)_d of Λ cut out by the idempotents σ₀(e_x), with kernel F^{d+1}A(x,y) (σ_piece_surj, finrank_piece_le).

    For A itself, posFiltA is the filtration J^n of the source (FilteredA.lean), and the radical lies in J¹ because the degree-zero part of A₀ has no nonzero nilpotents (lenA0_noNil). This gives the literal Lemma 3.7 (IndSkeleton.rayDegree_J).

            Lemma 3.7 (lem:ray-degree) for the categorical filtration F^dA(x,y) = J^d(P_y,P_x) (posFiltA): in every corner, the pieces A₀(x,y)_d (cut out by the initial forms of the idempotents) have dimension at most one; a nonzero element of degree d has nonzero initial form spanning A₀(x,y)_d; two nonzero elements have the same ray iff they have the same degree; every nonzero piece is reached; and U_{r'} ⊊ U_r forces deg_J r' > deg_J r.
